facts.raw_span: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for: synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

concepts.why: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, and positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support the diagnosis of apocrine carcinoma.
The positive staining for estrogen receptor and GATA3 antibodies, and the presence of cytokeratin8/18-positive tumor cells in the sentinel lymph node suggest a possible breast cancer origin.

The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, and the detection of tumor cells in the sentinel lymph node, along with the absence of primary or secondary tumors in imaging studies, suggest a possible cutaneous metastasis.
The presence of tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, and positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, and GCDFP15 antibodies support the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma.

The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, and the detection of tumor cells in the sentinel lymph node, along with the absence of primary or secondary tumors in imaging studies, suggest a possible carcinoma of unknown primary.
The presence of multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor-positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration supports the diagnosis of apocrine gland tumor.

rationales.F01: Subcutaneous node is non-specific, but could be related to apocrine gland tumor or carcinoma

rationales.F07: Indian file pattern and basophilic nuclei are characteristic of apocrine carcinoma
rationales.F08: Positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies supports apocrine carcinoma
rationales.F10: GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration supports apocrine carcinoma
rationales.F11: Isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells in sentinel lymph node suggests metastasis, which could be from apocrine carcinoma or other carcinomas

frontier_selector.rationale: Apocrine Carcinoma best explains the findings, including dermal tumor infiltration, Indian file pattern, and positivity for specific antibodies, without strong contradictions.
